title: Settings registry
description: The addressable settings of one program (desktop experience, section 10.3; docs/architecture/tur-settings.md). Every settings page and every row on it has an address, page[#row], that keeps its meaning for ever and is never reused. A program with addressable content ships one registry file, installed under /usr/share/tur/settings/; tur-settings merges them, searches them and resolves an address to its owner. The loader in desktop/apps/tur-settings (src/registrydata.cpp) and the check desktop/ci/registry.py are authoritative. They also enforce what this schema cannot express: a page address occurs once in all loaded registries and a row identifier once on its page; a row's section is one its page declares; an address named by replaced_by exists and is not itself removed; a page in the kde namespace says how it is opened; and an address that was ever on the main branch is still there, marked removed if it is gone.

text.description: A source string in British English, translated with the program. Not blank, at most 200 characters, no control characters.

keywords.description: Words a person might search for that are not in the title. Source strings, translated with the program.

page_address.description: The address of a page: a namespace, tur or kde, and one or more segments. Lower-case ASCII; never translated; never shown outside developer mode.

row_id.description: The identifier of a row on its page; the part of an address after '#'.

address.description: A page, or a row on a page.

section.description: A titled group of rows on a page. Sections are not addressable: a row that moves to another section keeps its address.

change.description: What changing the setting is, for the assistant. class is the action class of the AI control layer: 0 observe, 1 reversible, 2 consequential, 3 system-critical, 4 the assistant may open the page and point at the row and nothing more. Pointing at a setting is always class 0. tool names the typed tool that changes it, when one exists.

source.description: What backs a row: where its value is read from, or what a change is given to. available says whether that exists in the system today; a row whose source is not available is shown as unavailable and is never given a made-up value. waits_for says what is missing.

oneOf.description: A key of a file of KEY=VALUE lines, or the whole file.
A property or a method of a D-Bus service.
What a program prints. The program is an absolute path and its arguments a vector; nothing is given to a shell.
A key of one of KDE's configuration files, as kreadconfig6 names it.
What the desktop tells every program, through Qt: for example whether it prefers a light or a dark scheme.
Something the program that shows the row knows by itself: its own version, a text it carries.
A row that leads somewhere else: it opens another address.

locator.description: For a row of a program TUR does not write: how the control is found in that program's accessibility tree (desktop experience, section 10.4). Tried in order: the accessibility identifier, then the role with the label looked up in the program's own translation catalogue. The locator and its test are task D-20; nothing resolves one yet.

kind.description: What the row is: a switch, a choice among a few, a number, a text, a list, an action (a button), or information that is only read.

status.description: available (the default), or removed: the row is gone and its address is kept so that it is never given to anything else.

allOf.description: Information is only read: there is nothing to change. Every other kind says what changing it is.

path.description: Where the page is in its program's list, from the top: ["P@x", "Privacy"]. The last item is the page's own title.

status.description: available (the default); planned: the address is reserved and the page is not built, so it cannot be opened; removed: the page is gone and its address is kept.

listed.description: False for a page that is in the list only while a feature is enabled. Default true.

open.description: For a page of a program TUR does not write: how it is opened. module is the identifier of a module of KDE System Settings, as `systemsettings --list` prints it; arguments are passed to it with --args.

verified_with.description: The version of the other program the page's entry and its locators were checked against, for example plasma-6.8.2.

licence.description: The SPDX identifier of the file, as a string: JSON has no comments.

program.description: The program the pages belong to: its application identifier, which is also the D-Bus well-known name on which it offers org.tur.Addressable1 at /org/tur/Addressable1. org.tur.Settings for tur-settings. For KDE System Settings, which offers no such interface, org.kde.systemsettings.
